2 3.

The petitioner has filed the suit calling in question the sale deed dated 24.08.1996 executed by the first to third respondents in favour of the fourth respondent essentially asserting that these respondents could not have executed the impugned sale deed.

The petitioner's case is that his father,
Mr.P.V.Palanivelu Modaliyar has inducted Mr.S.M.Kumaran, first to third respondents' father, as a tenant in the year 1965 under a registered lease deed which is also renewed in the year 1983,
and notwithstanding these circumstances which would show that the first to third respondents cannot have any title or interest in the subject property, they have executed the impugned sale deed.

As against these averments, the fourth respondent has filed written statement justifying the conveyance of title in her favour under the sale deed dated 24.08.1996 stating that her vendor and their ancestors are in possession of the subject property over 50-60 years prior to the sale deed and therefore the title.
4.

It is undisputed that during the pendency of the suit the subject property is acquired by the BMRCL and compensation payable is deposited in LAC No.75/2014 with the civil Court under the provisions of Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894.

The amendment proposed by the fourth respondent essentially relates to this fact and it is also contended that if M/s. BMRCL is not included as party defendant, the suit must be rejected for non- joinder of necessary party.
5.

This Court is not persuaded to opine that merely because the fourth respondent contends that the suit must be dismissed for non-joinder of necessary party, the amendment must be kept out when it is undisputed that the subject property is acquired by BMRCL and the amount in deposit under Section 30 of the Land Acquisition Act 1894 can only be disbursed subject to the outcome of the present suit.
As such, the petition stands rejected.
It is needless to observe that with the writ petition being now disposed of, the petitioner will be at liberty to file rejoinder.
